Rigid monogamy can turn fear and possession into moral law. Free love without inner work can distribute the same fear across a larger spreadsheet. A relationship label doesn’t release childhood panic, comparison, abandonment terror, or the wish to control another person.

I discuss this at length in The Romance Guide, but here I’ll try to touch on the problem because it relates to how people operate in a community setting where people are much closer together. The simple problem is that jealousy can infiltrate either system.

Having a monogamy system set up rigidly can come from fear and be very possessive. Having a free love system can ALSO come from the same place. Just because people say they’re in one or the other kind of relationship, that doesn’t mean the underlying issues of childhood, jealousy, comparison, fear of being left, control, etc. go away.

Because eventually a community will re-organize itself around attraction and pair-bonding. Not like in a big city where two people can break up, move to different neighborhoods and have different friends. In a commune, a couple will affect the whole group: their loyalties, where they sleep, how they work, where their kids go, who their friends are.

The discussion generally goes straight to “should a group be monogamous or free-love?” but as I discuss in my Romance Guide , this is one level too late in the conversation. The real issue is that, in close quarters, jealousy gets magnified, and can corrupt either system.

Rigid monogamy can become an expression of fear, trying to possess another person and control their life. But “free love” can just be an attempt to spread that fear out over a larger spreadsheet. Neither relationship form will magically dissolve the fear/jealousy/possession that comes up from the unhealed child within each of the partners.

But each couple can decide for themselves what configuration they want to try, what agreements they want to make, and work to receive support for uncovering that material.

2. No one’s basic access to the community (housing, kids, etc…) should be tied to their being in a specific romantic agreement.

3. Look to long-experimenting groups like ZEGG and Tamera for inspiration as to how to relate romantically within a community setting.

4. Agree that jealousy cannot be the governor of the group, and to support each other to expose and release it. This is the only non-negotiable.

Agree to disagree on the rest, while still holding the basic support of the group and its need for basic group boundaries.
outputs.u6-emuB:
Intentional communities will either start or eventually reorganize around attraction and pair-bonding. It’s unavoidable. It’s much easier to separate from an ex when there’s an entire city between yourselves; when there’s only 30 people, a couple’s dynamics affect the entire community.

Most people argue about this on the level of “monogamy vs free love” (see my Romance Guide for the long version of this answer), but I think that starts one level too late. When people live in close proximity, any system gets infected by jealousy.

People can dress it up in the rigid morality of “monogamy” or spread it out in a spreadsheet of “free love”, but unless people do the work to release it, their fear will express as jealousy, possession, and any number of other typically childish behaviors, regardless of the relationship form .

As a community, I would allow for multiple relationship forms between different couples. Different people have different agreements they need to make to feel safe and explorative in their relationships, and they should be supported in doing the work to make those agreements conscious.

However, I would make sure that no one’s housing, children, community membership, or access to other necessities depends on any relationship form.

Communities like ZEGG and Tamera have been experimenting in this area for decades, and have some interesting solutions. The important thing is that the community does not pretend that the erotic is unimportant.

Finally, I would not allow for jealousy to be the governor of any relationship form. Jealousy must be released. This is the one non-negotiable, in my opinion.

Of course, different people will have different opinions on this, and the group will need to find ways of supporting each other, while setting boundaries on basic behaviors.
